title: Consciousness research is having an AI moment. Will the hype help the field?
excerpt: The idea of AI sentience is drawing more focus to consciousness science. But some researchers aren’t sure that’s a good thing.
content_html:
As artificial-intelligence systems become more and more sophisticated, the question of whether they might become conscious is capturing the public’s attention — and is sending tech firms to hire philosophers. The problem is, researchers still haven’t agreed on what gives rise to consciousness in humans, let alone an AI chatbot.

If AI becomes conscious: here’s how researchers will know

So some scientists who study human consciousness — the subjective state of being aware of yourself and your surroundings — worry that all the hype will make it harder to find answers. “What we might see is a sort of capture of consciousness research by the AI sector, where less emphasis is placed on the neuroscience and philosophy of how consciousness happens in real brains, and more on looking for computational ‘signatures’ of consciousness in AI,” says Anil Seth, a consciousness scientist at the University of Sussex near Brighton, UK. Seth and others think that consciousness is very unlikely outside of biological organisms and are frustrated by the focus on AI. Some are suspicious of AI firms’ hype, and think that there should be more investigation of how the humanization of chatbots could affect people negatively.

But there are researchers who think that tech firms’ obsession with consciousness is a boon for a field that was not taken seriously as a scientific endeavour for years. They see the hype as bringing more interest and, importantly, more funding.

Running into problems

Earlier this month, it became clear that determining whether an AI system is sentient will be extremely challenging without knowing more about human consciousness. Researchers at AI firm Anthropic, in San Francisco, California, posted a non-peer-reviewed study suggesting that they had found something in the company’s large language model (LLM) Claude that is comparable to conscious thoughts in humans.

Consciousness theory slammed as ‘pseudoscience’ — sparking uproar

By measuring patterns in Claude’s processing, they uncovered words that Claude ‘thought’ about as it worked through a request but did not necessarily include in its output. The authors compare this internal activity with the brain’s ‘global workspace’, a concept borrowed from one of the most popular theories of human consciousness. The global workspace theory (GWT) posits that information enters human consciousness when it is broadcast across the brain, in a type of processing hub for the mind.

The researchers don’t claim that their finding means Claude is capable of subjective experience. But critics were quick to point out that consciousness researchers don’t all agree on the existence of a global workspace in humans. The GWT also doesn’t formally define global workspace, which makes it hard to identify the phenomenon in entities such as chatbots, wrote Tim Bayne, a philosopher at Monash University in Melbourne, Australia, in an article about the Anthropic work for The Conversation.

Some in the field, including Erik Hoel, a consciousness researcher and lead scientist at non-profit research organization Bicameral Labs, in Boston, Massachusetts, say that running into such roadblocks can be a good thing for science. “Let’s use the problems in AI consciousness research to figure out what’s wrong with the stuff in [human] consciousness research and fix it,” Hoel wrote in a blogpost on 13 July.

content_html_zh:
随着人工智能系统变得越来越复杂，它们是否可能变得有意识的问题引起了公众的关注，并促使科技公司聘请哲学家。 问题是，研究人员对于人类意识的产生原因尚未达成一致，更不用说人工智能聊天机器人了。

如果人工智能变得有意识：研究人员将通过以下方式知道

因此，一些研究人类意识（意识到自己和周围环境的主观状态）的科学家担心，所有的炒作都会让找到答案变得更加困难。 英国布莱顿附近苏​​塞克斯大学的意识科学家 Anil Seth 表示：“我们可能会看到人工智能领域对意识研究的一种捕捉，较少强调神经科学和意识如何在真实大脑中发生的哲学，而更多地关注人工智能中意识的计算‘签名’。” 赛斯和其他人认为，在生物有机体之外，意识是不太可能存在的，并且对人工智能的关注感到沮丧。 一些人对人工智能公司的炒作表示怀疑，并认为应该对聊天机器人的人性化如何对人们产生负面影响进行更多调查。

但也有研究人员认为，科技公司对意识的痴迷对于这个多年来并未被认真对待的科学领域来说是一个福音。 他们认为炒作会带来更多的兴趣，更重要的是，带来更多的资金。

遇到问题

本月早些时候，人们清楚地认识到，在不了解更多关于人类意识的情况下，确定人工智能系统是否具有感知能力将是极具挑战性的。 位于加利福尼亚州旧金山的人工智能公司 Anthropic 的研究人员发布了一项未经同行评审的研究，表明他们在该公司的大语言模型 (LLM) Claude 中发现了一些与人类有意识思维相当的东西。

意识理论被猛烈抨击为“伪科学”——引发轩然大波

通过测量克劳德处理过程中的模式，他们发现了克劳德在处理请求时“思考”过的单词，但不一定包含在其输出中。 作者将这种内部活动与大脑的“全局工作空间”进行了比较，该概念借鉴了最流行的人类意识理论之一。 全局工作空间理论（GWT）认为，当信息在大脑中传播时，信息就会进入人类意识，大脑是一种心灵处理中心。

研究人员并没有声称他们的发现意味着克劳德有能力进行主观体验。 但批评者很快指出，意识研究人员并不都同意人类存在全球工作空间。 澳大利亚墨尔本莫纳什大学的哲学家蒂姆·贝恩 (Tim Bayne) 在 The Conversation 发表的一篇关于人类工作的文章中写道，GWT 也没有正式定义全局工作空间，这使得识别聊天机器人等实体中的现象变得困难。

该领域的一些人士，包括马萨诸塞州波士顿非营利性研究组织两院实验室的意识研究员和首席科学家埃里克·霍尔（Erik Hoel）表示，遇到此类障碍对科学来说可能是一件好事。 “让我们利用人工智能意识研究中的问题来找出（人类）意识研究中的问题并加以解决，”霍尔在 7 月 13 日的博文中写道。
